lawyer:
Md Soyeb Khan, AAG ------ For the Petitioners. 
Md Khalilur Rahman with Mr Khalilur Rahman (Helal), Advocates ------ For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Government of Bangladesh, and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Mohsina Rahman alias Joya ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
At the instance of defendant-respondent-petitioners, Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and decree complained of in the petition moved in Court today should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 24-11-2005 (decree signed on 30-11-2005) in Title Appeal No. 403 of 2003 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 31-8-2005 (decree signed on 5-10-2005) passed in Title Suit No. 191 of 2005 by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Dohar Court, Dhaka dismissing the suit.

3. The relevant facts for disposal of this Rule are that the present opposite party as plaintiff, Mrs Mohsina Rahman alias Joya, filed Title Suit No. 6 of 2005 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Dohar Court, Dhaka on transfer which was renumbered as the title Suit No. 191 of 2005 against the present petitioners contending that Ahsan Ullah Bhuiyan was the owner and possessor of 7 decimals of land appertaining to CS Khatian Nos. 168 and 16 and CS Dag Nos. 423, 433 and 434 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 882 and SA Dag No. 2047 containing a land measuring 7 decimals and also corresponding to SA Khatian No. 883 and Dag No. 2048 measuring a land of 8 decimals (hereinafter described as "the suit land") .The said Ahsan Ullah Bhuiyan transferred the aforementioned total 15 decimals of land to the mother of the plaintiff, Meherunnessa Chowdhury, by registered sale deed being No. 54 dated 28-8-1962 and thereafter handed over possession of the suit land. The said Meherunnessa Chowdhury while was possessing the suit land mutated in her name with the relevant government offices by opening a separate holding number and paying rent (খাজনা) to the government.

4. She later on transferred the suit land to her daughter, the present plaintiff-appellant-opposite party by executing 2(two) registered heba-bil-ewaz deeds being Nos. 44231 and 4432 both dated 12-4-1979 and the present plaintiff-opposite party went into possession thereon. Thereafter the present opposite party mutated the suit land in her name through a Jamabagh Case No. 2102 (N) C1 of 1979-80 and also mutated her name through another Jamabagh Case No. 2133 (N) P1 of 1979-80 and thereby she became absolute owner of the suit land and paying rent (খাজনা) to the government, the present petitioners, upto 1410 BS. She then made a new holding by registering with the Dhaka City Corporation and obtained all utility connections such as, gas, electricity and water line in her name. In course of time she demolished her existing old building in order to construct a multistoried building for commercial and residential purposes and obtained Rajuk approved plan and thereafter constructed a 16 storied building for residential and commercial purposes. In the meantime, the suit land was mutated in the name of the present plaintiff-opposite party Mrs Mohsina Rahman alias Joya in the Mohanagar Surveys (DP of such Parcha).

5. It is further stated that when the present plaintiff-opposite party was an absolute owner and possessor went to the relevant authority on 13-12-2004 to pay the annual rent (খাজনা) but she came to know that during the last Revenue Survey the suit property has been mutated in the name of the present defendant-petitioners government and she was denied to pay rent (খাজনা) for the suit land. After being confirmed about the recording of the Revenue Survey (SA) in the name of government, the present plaintiff-opposite party filed the present suit for declaring the recording in RS Khatian in the name of Government as illegally and unlawfully made by the office of the government by a gross mistake and not binding upon the present-opposite party.

6. The present defendant-petitioner, the government appeared and contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint and contending that the suit land was correctly recorded in the name of the government and since the land is recorded in favour of the Bangladesh Government all title and interest have been vested upon the government.

7. The trial court on consideration of the material evidence on records adduced by the parties both by deposition in the court and also through documentary evidences dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 31-8-2005 (decree signed on 5-9-2005). Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment the present plaintiff-opposite party preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 403 of 2005 before learned District Judge, Dhaka. The said appeal was thereafter transferred to the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka who after hearing both the parties passed its judgment dated 24-11-2005 allowing the appeal thereby decreeing the suit, hence the present petitioners-Government filed this revisional application and the instant Rule was issued thereupon.

8. Mr Md Soyeb Khan, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the petitioners submits that the impugned judgment and decree is not a proper judgment of reversal in the eye of law as the learned Appellate Court has not explained the reason to reverse the judgment of the trial court, therefore, the present Rule should be made absolute. The learned Assistant Attorney General further submits that the learned trial court below rightly held that the present plaintiff-opposite party has failed to prove that the original vendor Ahsan Ullah Bhuiyan sold the property to the predecessor of the present plaintiff-opposite party without providing any document as to the CS Recorded tenant, as such, the predecessor of present plaintiff-opposite party failed to prove the change of title of the suit property and, as such, recording of the suit property in the RS Survey in favour of the present defendant-petitioners, is not illegal or unlawful.

9. He also submits that the plaintiff-opposite party as being plaintiff of the suit mentioned nothing in the plaint about the change of title i.e. name of the CS recorded tenant from whom the said Ahsan Ullah Bhuiyan obtained his title, therefore, the plaintiff has utterly failed to prove its case but the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka erroneously passed the impugned order without considering above matters and thereby the learned Appellate Court committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside and the Rule should be made absolute. He also submits that the trial court rightly held that from the exhibit 4 and 4(3) which are the photocopy of the SA Khatian Nos. 882 and 883 containing that the previous khatians 1163 and 1164 indicates those as CS Khatians but except mentioning CS Khatian the plaintiff failed to prove the same by any scrap of papers but the learned Appellate Court below failed to apply its judicious mind and thereby reversed the findings of the trial court by committing an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

10. He further submits that in the present proceeding of the suit the learned trial court passed the order No. 14 dated 21-5-2005 appointing an Advocate Commissioner to submit a report after obtaining statement of the concerned lawyer and accordingly on 1-6-2005 the learned Advocate Commissioner submitted its report but he was not called in as a witness thus the defendant-petitioners did not have any opportunity to cross-examine as to the report which is illegal and unacceptable thus the finding of the Lower Appellate Court by the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. In support of his above contention he referred to a case of Abdul Noor (Md) alias Gunnu Mia and another vs. Makhan Mia alias Md Laisuzzaman reported in 60 DLR (AD) at page 39 which reads as follows:-

"Code of Civil Procedure (V of 1908) Order XXVI, rule 14(12) new line Since the Advocate Commissioner did not depose before the trial court nor the Court called him as witness his report was not admitted in evidence. In that stage of the matter, the High Court Division was not justified in relying on the same and reversing the judgment of the trial court."

11. As such he submits that the learned Appellate Court below committed an error of law. The learned Assistant Attorney General also submits that SA Rerecord has a presumptive value but the RS Record has no presumptive value. In support of his said contention he submits a case of Halima Begum vs Syed Ahmed reported in 21 DLR 854 which reads as follows:-

"The presumption of correctness as to CS record of right is not certainly available with regard to this State Acquisition Khatians. There is no presumption of correctness in respect of the State Acquisition Khatians as it is to be found in case of CS Khatians in pursuance of the provision under section 103-B of the Bengal Tenancy Act".

12. On the basis of the above submissions the learned Assistant Attorney General prayed to set aside the impugned judgment and decree and to make the Rule absolute.

13. The rule has been opposed by the plaintiff-appellant-opposite party.

14. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party along with Mr Md Khalilur Rahman (Helal), the learned Advocate contended that the original suit filed by the present-plaintiff-opposite party as plaintiff for a declaration that the suit land has been mistakenly and arbitrarily recorded in the name of the present defendant petitioner, Government because the suit land was correctly recorded in CS Khatian Nos. 168 and 16 and Dag Nos. 724, 733 and 734 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 882 and SA Dag No. 2047 measuring land of 0.07 acres and also SA Khatian No. 883 and SA Dag No. 2048 measuring land of 0.08 acres making total measuring land of 0.15 acres in favour of the present-plaintiff-opposite party.

15. It is also contended that the present plaintiff-petitioner got an absolute ownership on the suit land by way of 2 heba-bil-ewaz deeds being deed Nos. 4431 and 4432 both registered on 28-4-1997. The opposite party's mother got the said land from the SA recorded tenant namely Ahsan Ullah Bhuiyan by a sale deed No. 5456 dated 23-8-1962 who obtained his title in course of different transaction from the CS recorded tenant. On the basis of the above transaction the present opposite party got an absolute ownership on the suit land and mutated her name and paid rent (খাজনা) to the concerned government offices until the year of 2004.

16. Having got an absolute ownership the suit land was registered with Dhaka City Corporation by opening a new holding number and she got all utility connections and she has been living for a quite long time in the suit property. At certain point of time she demolished the exciting building on the land in order to construct a multistoried building and applied to the Rajuk for obtaining an approval plan. Subsequently, the present opposite party constructed a 16 storied building the commercial and residential uses. On 13-12-2004 and 28-12-2004 the present plaintiff-opposite party went to the concerned government office to pay rent (খাজনা) wherein the authority of the government office refused to take rent (খাজনা) from her. Hence the suit was filed.

17. In course of trial by the learned Assistant Judge, Dohar Court, Dhaka sought a report to be submitted by an Advocate Commissioner and Advocate Commissioner submitted its report on 1-6-2005 which became the part of the record. After hearing both the parties the trial court dismissed the suit on the finding that the plaintiff-opposite party failed to prove her case but the learned Appellate Court reversed the judgment of the trial court on appeal, hence this revisional application.

18. Mr. Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that the sale deed No. 5456 dated 20-8-1962 the predecessor of the opposite party Meherunnessa Chowdhury became absolute owner of the suit land measuring 0.15 acres of land from the holder of rayati right Ahsan Ullah Bhuiyan who acquired the right on the suit land in the following manner:—

"ALHAJ AHSANULLAH BHUIYAN son of late Mvi Jonab Ali Bhuiyan of Village Binnapaid, Police Station Monorhardi, District Dacca at present residing at 258, New Circular Road, Magbazar under Police Station Tejgaon, Dacca by faith Muslim, by profession businessman hereinafter termed as the Vendor (which expression unless excluded by or repugnant to the subject or context shall be deemed to include his heir, executor, administrator, legal representative or assign) of the OTHER PART;

WHEREAS the lands of Khatian No. 168 of Mouza Dhanmondi was held and owned in raiyati jote right by one Khedu Nunia and was correctly recorded in CS as such and who by registered sale deed dated 5-4-1929 sold the said land to Surya Kumar Bose who purchased the same in his own name and in the benami of Jaanada Bashini Ghose;

AND WHEREAS the sons and legal heir of Khedu Nunia having failed to make over possession of the said land to the said Surya Kumar Bose, he instituted TS No. 65 of 1930 in the Court of Second Additional Subordinate Judge, Dacca and got a decree for khas possession thereof;

AND WHEREAS the sons of Khedu Nunia preferred Title Appeal No. 317/31 against the judgment and decree of TS No. 65 of 1930 which was rejected and Surya Kumar Bose got into possession of the said land;

AND WHEREAS the lands of khatian No. 16 of Mouza Dhanmondai was recorded in the name of one Dukhini Bewa who surrendered the same in favour of the land-lord, the Dacca Nowab Estate and the latter settled it out to Surya Kumar Bose who while owning and possessing the lands of Khatian No. 16 of Mouza Dhanmondai in raiyati jote right for more than 12 years sold the same to Wazuddin and Mahmuda Begum by registered sale deed dated 18-9-1952.

19. AND WHEREAS Surya Kumar Bose died leaving behind his widow Monorama Bose and six sons Jogesh Chandra Bose, Swadwesh Ranjan Bose, Sudhir Kumar Bose, Sukumar Bose, Narayan Chandra Bose and Satish Chandra Bose as his legal heirs to the lands of Khatian No. 168 . And in order to make the title of the owners to the land free from all possible claims the legal heirs of benamdar Jaanada Bashini Ghose, Sachindra Kumar Ghose and two other executed a registered deed on 25-12-1952 whereby they relinquished all claim to the lands of Khatian No. 168 in favour of Monorama Bose and her aforesaid six sons;

AND WHEREAS Monorama Bose and her sons and Wazuddin, Mahmuda Begum while thus absolutely seized and possessed of the lands of Khatian No. 168 and 16 respectively, for valid and valuable considerations sold the entire lands of Khatian No. 168 and 16 by registered sale deed dated 25-12-1952 to the Vendor and 19 other persons clearly demarcating in the map annexed with and forming part of the said sale deed the specific plots sold to each of the 20 purchasers and according to the demarcation and specification in the said map plot No. 6 to the Vendor:

AND WHEREAS the VENDOR while thus owning and possessing said plot No. 6 being in urgent need of money sold the same to Mvi. Mofazzal Hussain by a sale deed dated 2-4-1955 followed by a registered agreement by the said purchaser to reconvey the land in favour of the VENDOR;

AND WHEREAS in conformity with the agreement Mvi. Mofazzal Hussain by a registered sale deed dated 31-3-1958 reconvened the land to the VENDOR;

AND WHEREAS the VENDOR thus absolutely seized and possession of the land of plot No. 6 being in need of money to finance his business proposed to sell the 8 kathe 13 chataks of land of plot No. 6 and the PURCHASER offered a price of Rs. 15,000 for the same and the VENDOR having found it to be the highest price available in the market accepted the offer of the PURCHASER".

20. From the above description of the previous CS owner the plaintiff opposite party established its ownership but the trial court without considering the above records in the documents dismissed the suit but the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka after perusing the records decreed the suit legally and validly, therefore, the learned appellate court below by passing the impugned judgment and order has committed no error of law thus the Rule is liable to be discharged.

21. The learned Advocate for the opposite party further submits that the present petitioners after considering the aforesaid history of the recorded owners of the suit property recorded in the name of the present plaintiff-opposite party and also in the Mohanagor Survey recorded the suit land in the name of the present-opposite party, as such, the opposite party has proved the change of ownership and title on the suit land but mistakenly and incorrectly RS record was recorded in the name of Government without any basis and without giving any opportunity to the present-opposite party before changing from the SA Khatian to RS Khatian which is violation of section 90 of the Evidence Act as such, after evaluation of the aforementioned record of rights in favour of the opposite party the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka by the impugned judgment decreed the suit and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and thereby committed no error of law thus the Rule is liable to be discharged.

22. The learned Advocate of the opposite party further submits in reply to the submissions made by the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the petitioners that the report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner pursuant to the order of the trial court has become a part of the record under Order XXVI, rule 10(2) of the Civil Procedure, even though the Advocate Commissioner was not examined or cross-examined. Moreover the trial court failed to mention a single word about the report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner which became part of the record, as such, the judgment and decree dismissing the suit has passed unlawfully and it has been correctly set aside by the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate court below.

23. The learned Advocate further submits that the relevant government authorities after examining the documents presented for recording the SA Khatian in favour of the present plaintiff-opposite party the present petitioners is to be estopped from denying such record of right by rerecording the RS Record in the name of the present defendant petitioners under the principle of promissory estoppel as provided in the Evidence Act. Thus the Rule is liable to be discharged.

24. He further submits that if there is conflict between the records of right i.e. SA, RS and BS then the latest record of right should prevail over any other record. In support of his contention he submitted a case of Fatema Khatun vs Fazil Mia reported in 21 BLD 14 = 6 BLC which reads as follows: State acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (XXVIII of 1951) section-144A.

25. In the event of a conflict between the old Record of right and recent record of right, recent record of right would prevail inasmuch as presumption of the record of right loses its weight with the passage of time and entry in the subsequent khatian (Para-31)".

26. On the basis of the above submissions the learned Advocate prayed to discharge the Rule.

27. After considering the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the parties and also perusing the application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure along with the annexures, judgment and decree, particularly the impugned judgment passed on 30-11-2005, it appears to me that the suit land appertaining to CS Khatian No. 168 and 16 and CS Dag Nos. 724, 733 and 734 corresponding to SA Dag Nos. 882 and 883 measuring total land of 0.15 acres of land was originally owned and possessed by one Ahsan Ullah Bhuiyan through a long transfer of rayati tenancy as mentioned in the documents executed in favour of Meherunnessa Chowdhury, the mother of the present plaintiff-opposite party. The said Meherunnessa Chowdhury while was an absolute owner and possessor of the suit land mutated her name after complying all required formalities for recording the suit land in her name and paying rent (খাজনা) to the Government. She transferred the suit land to her daughter by 2(two) registered deeds of heba-bil-ewaz being Nos. 4431 and 4432 both dated 14-4-1997. The present opposite party after becoming the possessor of the suit land mutated her name with the relevant Government Authority and duly paid rent (খাজনা) with the said authority having acquired record of right in the State Acquisition (SA) Survey in favour of the predecessor of the opposite party on the basis of the above record of right her name was mutated pursuant to the Mutation Case No. 515-P-1 of 77-78 and 516-P-1 of 77-78 and enjoying the possession therefrom.

28. In presence of the above chain of title prevailing as to the ownership and record of right in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party, the Government has changed the record of right in favour of the Revisional Survey (RS) in favour of the government which caused filing of the present suit by the plaintiff-opposite party in the trial court.

29. Here, the question arises how, when and after following what procedure the concerned authority changed the RS Record of right from the name of the present plaintiff-opposite party in SA Record to the defendant-petitioner has not been mentioned anywhere in the record of the present case. It is true that the provision of law regarding burden of proof is the plaintiff has to prove its own case with the standard of balance of probability but the questions are whether the petitioners-Government produced any document in the courts to substantiate break of chain of title in order to change record of right and whether relevant government authorities have given any opportunity to the recorded owner to the suit land before changing the record of right from SA to RS? If it has not been done, it is apparent that plaintiff is not aware about the reason for such change. In my consideration burden of proof in the given circumstances is to be shifted from the plaintiff-opposite party to the defendant-petitioners who is the maker of the RS Record but there is nothing on record of this case as to the reason behind the change of the record of right from SA to RS in favour of the Government. I am sure that the relevant authority has not changed the record of right with a consideration to benefit the government rather it has been done randomly and without following any legal procedure for such change with a corrupt intention and such kind of silent corruptions are causing unnecessary huge number of litigations and sufferings to the holder of valid documents, thus, the laid administrative authorities should be held accountable.

30. Regarding the submission made by the learned advocate for the petitioners as to the change of title which needed to be proved by plaintiff-opposite party in the trial court. In such matter I consider that in the instant case the deeds or transductions from 1962 until 1997 have not been challenged by the Government or title deeds have not been invalidated, thus, the documents exhibited being exhibit Nos. 5, 7 and 7 (a) remained valid documents for the ownership of the suit land and without contradicting the validity of such documents a chain of title cannot be broken and thereby record of right in Revision Survey (RS) in favour of the Government cannot take way the title and right of the plaintiff opposite party from the suit land. It is well established principle that valid deeds are the principal documents for the ownership of a land and record of right under the Tenancy Rules , 1953 are to be considered as supporting documents and possession therefrom for creating entitlement on a land. So, the chain has not been broken to introduce any new record of right.

31. Regarding the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners as to the report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner and the case cited in support of such contentions reported in 60 DLR (AD) page 38, I consider that this is a case where Order XXVI, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure is more relevant law then Order XXVI, rule 42 of the Code of Civil Procedure as referred in the said case. In this regard I consider Order XXVI, rule 10(2) which reads as follows:-"

"10(2) the report of the Commissioner and the evidence taken by him (but not the evidence without the report) shall be evidence in the suit and shall form part of the record; but the Court or, with the permission of the Court, any of the parties to the suit may examine the Commissioner personally in open court touching any of the matters referred to him or mentioned in his report, or as to his report, or as to the manner in which he has made the investigation."

<u>32. From the above provision of law sub-rule (2) it appears that the report of the Commissioner becomes an evidence in the suit and form part of the rerecords and such, provision is mandatory provision, whereas, the second part of sub-rule (2) for giving an opportunity to examine the Commissioner personally in the open Court is matter of discretion of the trial court on his own motion or by a permission obtained by a party of the suit, therefore, I consider the decision as reported in 60 DLR (AD) is not applicable in the present case.</u>

33. Regarding the submission of the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the petitioners that the SA Record has no presumptive value but RS Rerecord has a presumptive value and reported case cited in 21 DLR 854 of this court I consider such decision is not incorrect because the process of SA Record has been conducted on the basis of the CS Record. In the present case the Government Authority who has given the S.A. Record in favour of the predecessor of the present plaintiff-opposite party must have examined or presumed to have examined the CS Record before giving the SA Record in favour of the opposite party. Once SA Record has been given after examining the previous holder of record of right in favour of the opposite party it cannot be taken away randomly or arbitrarily without considering the documents connecting to the suit land and without giving an opportunity for producing or adducing any document available for continuation of record of right. In this regard, I consider that it is evident from record that who has changed the record of right in favour of the Government has not done it for the benefit of the government but with a very corrupt intention and ill motive has done it.

34. Therefore, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge giving a full and thorough examination of the record of right to be continued in favour of the present plaintiff-opposite party but the trial court has utterly failed to consider important aspect of the case, like, the documents produced exhibited by the plaintiff and also the document of Advocate Commissioner sought by himself. As such, the learned Joint District Judge by passing the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-11-2005 in Title Appeal No. 403 of 2005 setting aside the judgment and decree of the Senior Assistant Judge, Dohar Court, Dhaka dated 31-8-2011 has committed no error of law. I am not inclined to interfere into the impugned judgment and decree.

35. Accordingly, I find no merit in the Rule.

36. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

37. Having passed the above decision of this court in the instant case, I would like to observe that the litigation and the concerned authorities of the government should consider whether the matter for entailment of a land and the supporting documents of record of right, including the previous record of right should be maintained containing in a single document in order to reduce the possible corruption and irregularities about the entitlement of a land which could help to reduce the number of litigations arising from the presently existing complicated system of entitlement and record of right for a land.

38. The office is directed to send down the Lower Court's Record with a copy of this judgment and order to the court concerned and another copy of the judgment and order to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka immediately.

End.
